nodes.name: Humanoid robot actuated joints (capability)
nodes.description: The capability to actuate commercial humanoid robot joints: rotary joints (hips/shoulders/knees), linear joints, and dexterous hand/finger actuation, at the torque density, backdrivability, precision, and unit cost humanoid programs require. Structural container per ADR-0004; the three sibling products below are alternative joint architectures.

targetContext.targetUseCase: Commercial humanoid robot programs (2025-2027 pilot-to-production wave)
targetContext.targetScale: 10k-100k+ robots/year per leading program target; ~30-50 actuated joints per robot
targetContext.targetPerformance: High torque density, low backlash, backdrivable or force-controlled joints

nodes.name: Rotary actuator joint (harmonic reducer)
nodes.description: Rotary humanoid joint module: strain-wave (harmonic) gear reducer + frameless torque motor + joint encoder + bearing + housing, integrated as a torque-dense rotary actuator. The architecture used for most rotary joints in current humanoid prototypes and early production runs.

nodes.name: Linear actuator joint (planetary roller screw)
nodes.description: Linear humanoid joint module: planetary roller screw + motor (frameless or integrated) + sensing, converting rotary drive to high-force linear motion for legs/torso. Selected by several leading humanoid programs for high load joints; supply story dominated by precision thread-grinding capacity.

nodes.name: Dexterous hand actuation
nodes.description: Hand/finger actuation for humanoids: tendon/cable drives or micro linear drives, micro motors and leadscrews, integrated tactile/force sensing, packaged at finger scale. The least mature of the three joint architectures; designs vary widely across programs.

edges.claim: Harmonic rotary joints are the dominant architecture for humanoid rotary DoF. Product->Capability per ADR-0004.
Roller-screw linear joints serve high-load humanoid DoF in several leading programs.
Dexterous hand actuation covers the hand/finger DoF of the capability.
